# ⚡ dsh-codex-sync
**Two-way Codex↔DSH bridge: skills from `~/.codex/skills`, session import with workspace attach, liv
e MCP mirroring of `mcp_servers`, and a Codex-side reverse MCP installer.**
*2-way project chat sync · Live Skills mount · Auto MCP mirroring · Native modern UI*

English •
简体中文

> **This repository is our own build of the plugin, adapted to our DSH runtime.**
> It is based on /

forked from **Walvez/dsh-codex-sync**
> (MIT © 2026 Walvez) — see Credits & upstream attribution.
>

What we changed and why: docs/LOCAL-ADAPTATION.md.
> Upstream npm package `dsh-codex-sync` belongs
to the original author and is **not** this build.
🎛️ Native Sync Settings Modal
📍 Sidebar Workspace Trigger
📥 Import from Codex by Project
📤 Export DSH Chats to Codex
## 🤔 Why dsh-codex-sync?

When using OpenAI Codex, developers build up significant workflow assets:
1. **Rich project chat his

tories** with complete code contexts, architecture decisions, and debugging steps;
2. **Custom Skill

s libraries** under `~/.codex/skills` with tailored instructions and scripts;
3. **Configured MCP to
olchains** for databases, web searches, and browser automation.

When adopting or exploring **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)**, developers typically face major friction:
- *
*Lost conversation history**: Incompatible session formats prevent resuming past Codex tasks in DSH;
- **Configuration duplication and drift**: Skills and MCP servers must be manually recreated and ma

intained in two separate tools;
- **One-way dead ends**: Most migration scripts are one-time destruc
tive copies that offer no clean way to safely bring DSH continuations back to Codex.
**`dsh-codex-sync` eliminates this friction completely.** It is not a throwaway migrator, but a prod
uction-grade, continuous two-way bridge between Codex and DSH.
## ✨ Key Highlights

### 1. 💬 Two-Way Safe Project Chat Portability (Codex ⇄ DSH)
- **Import from Codex**:
- Browse conve

rsations grouped by workspace folder in an intuitive project tree;
- Preserves user prompts, assista

nt outputs, reasoning traces, and tool-call trajectories;
- Automatically attaches imported sessions

to matching workspaces for **seamless continuation**;
- Incremental re-import: Codex conversations
continued after the initial import are marked as `updated` and append only new turns without creatin

g duplicate sessions.
- **Export to Codex**:
- Export DSH native conversations or continuations back

into Codex;
- Automatically matches Codex's workspace catalog, gracefully locking unknown directori

es to prevent orphan threads;
- Creates clean, standalone Codex rollouts (`history_mode: legacy`) an

d SQLite index entries **without modifying or overwriting original Codex histories**;
- View and con

tinue chats in Codex immediately after restarting the Codex app.
- **Sub-Agent Thread Filtering**:
-

Hides internal sub-agent threads by default to keep the conversation list focused;
- Easily expand
and nest sub-agents under parent threads for selective, independent export.

### 2. ⚡ Live First-Class Skills Mounting
- Mounts `~/.codex/skills/*/SKILL.md` directly into DSH's
**Zero-restart updates**: Edit a skill file on disk, and DSH recognizes the change on the next turn.

### 3. 🔌 Automated Bidirectional MCP Mirroring
- **Codex → DSH**: Watches `~/.codex/config.toml` liv

e, dynamically mirroring `[mcp_servers.*]` to DSH with conflict avoidance and stderr silencing;
- **
DSH → Codex (Reverse Bridge)**: Single-command setup (`npx dsh-codex-sync codex-install`) equips you
r Codex agent with tools to search, inspect, and install DSH plugins.

### 4. 🎨 Native Modern UI Experience
- **Adaptive Sidebar Trigger**: Sits right beside the workspace

header when expanded, and aligns below the search button when collapsed;
- **Centered Modal Panel**
: High-contrast, backdrop-blurred settings card with intuitive action cards, real-time switch feedba

ck, and zero UI cutoff;
- **Polished Design Integration**: Uses native DSH design tokens (`--dsw-ali
as-*`), pure CSS transitions with zero hover artifacts, and responsive text truncation.
## 🧭 Supported DSH versions
Version pinning lives in `package.json` → `peerDependencies["@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client"] = "^0.0.1

-rc.1 || ^0.2.0-rc.2"`,
which is what the DSH install gate (`evaluatePluginCompatibility()` in `@dee
pseek-ai/dsh-app-boot`) checks.
| DSH runtime | Status | Evidence |
| **`0.2.1-rc.2`** | ✅ **Verified on our machine** (Linux, `web` profile) | 61/61 tests; cold boot o
n an isolated `DSH_HOME`; client bundle served; 5 mirrored Codex MCP servers; 123-session import dry

-run |
| `0.2.0-rc.2` | ✅ Verified by upstream v1.6.2 | upstream CI host-boot smoke |
| other `0.2.x

` | ⚠️ Allowed by the peer range, not re-verified here | — |
| `0.0.1-rc.1` … `0.0.x` | ⚠️ Legacy MC
P-client peer, unmaintained path | upstream `1.x` legacy peer |
- **Node.js**: `>=20`. Node 20 needs the `zstd` CLI for checksummed compression; Node 22+/24 uses na

tive Zstandard.
- If a future DSH release is rejected by the install gate, update the peer range (or

pin) here and re-run `npm test`.
- Nuance: `engines.dsh` is **not** set, so the gate evaluates the

peer range above; upstream used an exact
`0.2.0-rc.2` pin, which is exactly why `0.2.1-rc.2` refused
to install before this build.
